new_statements.rule_in_words: Bisu is a register-tone language (three level tones, low/mid/high, obligatory on every syllable). Stress exists but is called 'a relatively minor component' of the phonology and is said not to affect syllable structure; no rule for where word stress falls is given. The related evidence in Nishida 1973 (pp. 59-60) is that bound/subordinate morphemes after the main syllable are reduced ('weak utterances') in normal speech, which points to prominence on the main (root) syllable, but Nishida does not call this stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; Daic (Thai) loans have different syllable canons and borrowed rising tones (Person 2000; Nishida 1973 p. 59).
new_statements.domain_note: Word/syllable level, based on the author's fieldwork on Doi Chomphuu / Doi Pui Bisu (Chiang Rai, Thailand) = bisu1244; not the Laomian (Lancang) side of the retired code. Person cites Vacharee 1987 (Mahidol MA) as the description containing Bisu 'stress patterns'.
new_statements.identity_note: bisu1247 is a Glottolog bookkeeping entry, not a language: it is the retired ISO 639-3 code [bii] 'Bisu', split by change request 2007-092 (effective 2008-01-14) into Bisu [bzi] = bisu1244 (Thailand Bisu, incl. Laopin of Yunnan) and Laomian [lwm] = laom1237 (Lancang County, Yunnan). Glottolog lists zero descriptive references under bisu1247. The quoted statement (Person 2000) describes Doi Chomphuu/Doi Pui Bisu of Chiang Rai = bisu1244, whose check folder already holds the same file; it should be catalogued under bisu1244, not under the retired code (our rule that each source is filed under the language's current Glottolog code: a retired code does not make a separate language).

new_statements.quote: La courbe mélodique de la phrase Bisu se caractérise par une accentuation sur la syllabe finale des groupes syntaxiques, le Prédicat portant l'accentuation principale. En finale de phrase, on remarque une descente accentuelle. [p. 58, §7] — Un lexème autonome peut cependant être créé par l'affixation de plusieurs lexèmes avec une variation tonale sur le dernier (élévation du ton résultant d'une accentuation à valeur morphologique). [p. 58, §5.4] — A l'initiale de phrase, en position Sujet, le pronom personnel porte l'accentuation normale du Prédicat. Ex : "Je vais au marché" / ga kátʰɛ́ŋ / → [ ˈga kátʰɛ́ŋ ] [p. 78] — Les mots à préfixe [ ɑŋ- ] sont classés d'après l'initiale de la syllabe (accentuée) qui suit. [Tome 2, p. 3]
new_statements.translation: The melodic curve of the Bisu sentence is characterised by an accentuation on the final syllable of syntactic groups, the Predicate carrying the main accentuation. At the end of the sentence one notes an accentual fall. [p. 58, §7] — An autonomous lexeme can however be created by affixing several lexemes with a tonal variation on the last one (a raising of the tone resulting from an accentuation with morphological value). [p. 58, §5.4] — At the start of the sentence, in Subject position, the personal pronoun carries the accentuation that normally belongs to the Predicate. Ex. 'I go to the market' / ga kátʰɛ́ŋ / → [ ˈga kátʰɛ́ŋ ] [p. 78] — Words with the prefix [ɑŋ-] are alphabetised by the initial of the (accented) syllable that follows. [Tome 2, p. 3]

new_statements.relation_note: Agrees with Person 2000 (existing statement) that Bisu is a three-tone language in which stress is marginal and has no placement rule, and adds what Person lacks: the accent is phrase-level (final syllable of syntactic groups, main accent on the predicate, sentence-final fall), a morphological tone-raising accent on the last syllable of lexicalised compounds, and the note that the prefix ɑŋ- is unaccented relative to the following root syllable. Describes Ban Doy (Huai Chomphu, Mae Lao, Chiang Rai) Thailand Bisu = bisu1244, not the retired code as such. scanned coverage: Tome 1 PDF pp. 1-124 (thesis I-IX, 1-113) read and a full-text search for stress/accent; PDF 125-165 (thesis 114-154: rel…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bisu (Ban Doy) is a three-tone language (high/mid/low, tone obligatory in every syllable, §1 p. 37, §5 p. 56). Beaudouin gives no word-stress placement rule. What he calls accentuation is phrase-level: the final syllable of each syntactic group is accented, the predicate carries the main accent and the sentence ends with an accentual fall (§7 p. 58); a sentence-initial subject pronoun takes the predicate's accent (p. 78); sentence-final exclamative particles are reinforced by an accentuation he writes as high tone (p. 107). Morphologically, accent shows up as tone raising on the last syllable of a lexicalised compound (tsɔ̀ŋkɔ̀ŋ + wà → tsɔ̀ŋkɔ̀ŋwá 'wild boar', §5.4). The only word-internal hint is Tome 2 p. 3: the nominal prefix ɑŋ- is unaccented and the root syllable after it is 'accentuée'.
new_statements.exceptions: Tones in loans from Thai/Kammuang break Nishida's restriction of mid tone to open/nasal-final syllables (§5.2 p. 56); tone assimilation high>low in compounds (p. 57); mid tone written with no diacritic (p. IX, p. 56). Comparative §8 (pp. 59-66) treats Ban Ta Ko, Ban Pha Daeng, Ban Pwi Kham segmental differences only.
new_statements.identity_note: bisu1247 is the retired ISO 639-3 code [bii] "Bisu", split by change request 2007-092 (effective 2008-01-14) into Bisu [bzi] = bisu1244 (Thailand Bisu incl. Laopin) and Laomian [lwm] = laom1237. Beaudouin 1991 describes the Bisu of Ban Doy (Huai Chomphu, Amphoe Mae Lao, Chiang Rai), with comparative notes on Ban Ta Ko, Ban Pha Daeng and Ban Pwi Kham (§8 pp. 59-66) — all Thailand Bisu = bisu1244. Person 2000 (existing statement) describes Doi Chomphuu / Doi Pui Bisu, the same variety. Any catalog entry belongs under bisu1244, not the retired code.

Si l'accentuation reste marquée en début de phrase, des pauses de réflexion et des hésitations modifient très sensiblement le discours. Il est intéressant de noter que les interférences accent/ton sont ici très rares.' Phrase-level remark on read-aloud translations (sentence-initial accentuation persists; accent/tone interference rare); no word-stress rule; consistent…
